claims.text: Toughness retention in FCC high-entropy alloys is governed by element-specific nanoclustering at grain boundaries.
Separate Cr, Ni, and Mn nanoclusters at CrMnFeCoNi grain boundaries reduce grain-boundary cohesion.
Suppressing grain-boundary nanoclustering or redirecting segregation into pre-existing secondary phases increases retained toughness.
CrMnFeCoNi can have a single-phase FCC initial state.
Conventionally homogenized CrMnFeCoNi naturally develops detrimental Cr, Ni, and Mn nanoclustering at grain boundaries.
At intermediate deformation temperatures, loss of ductility in CrMnFeCoNi correlates with grain-boundary cracking.
A segregation-engineering heat treatment can induce Cr-rich secondary phases specifically at grain boundaries.
Pre-existing Cr-rich secondary phases divert fast segregation of principal elements away from grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary nanosegregation reduces cohesion and promotes early intergranular crack initiation.
Hosting segregating elements in Cr-rich secondary phases prevents excessive local grain-boundary clustering.
Preventing excessive grain-boundary clustering preserves grain-boundary integrity.
Segregation engineering shifts deformation toward intragranular dislocation slip or twinning.
The engineered CrMnFeCoNi samples will have a statistically significant increase in tensile fracture strain relative to the untreated baseline.
The engineered CrMnFeCoNi samples will have greater fracture toughness, including higher KIC, than the untreated baseline.
Microscopy of engineered samples will reveal reduced or redistributed grain-boundary nanoclustering.
The engineered samples will favor transgranular rather than intergranular fracture.
The proposed grain-boundary-nanoclustering mechanism applies to other single-phase FCC high-entropy alloys with similar compositions and microstructures.
At temperatures or strain rates dominated by diffusion, phase transformations, or extreme dislocation dynamics, grain-boundary nanoclustering becomes less important to toughness.

contradictions.description: The intervention intentionally forms Cr-rich secondary phases, whereas the stated applicability boundary describes the relevant alloys as single-phase. Unless 'single-phase' refers only to the pre-treatment state, the engineered state falls outside the stated boundary.
